notes.title: Under a Desert Sun: Seekers of the Cursed Vessel – Demo Launch
notes.notes: [h2][/h2][p][b]Hi everyone,[/b][/p][p]I’m Raymond. About a year ago, I started [i]Revolving Gear Studios[/i] to finally try my hand at making video games full-time. I’ve been a hobbyist developer for years, and I always dreamed of building something bigger and more focused. That’s where this new Action RPG was born: [b]Under a Desert Sun: Seekers of the Cursed Vessel[/b].[/p][p]The [b]Under a Desert Sun[/b] name might sound familiar — it comes from a small VR project I made years ago. I loved the world-building so much that I realized there were still plenty of stories left to tell in that universe.[/p][p]Why an Action RPG, you might ask? Before starting anything, I thought long and hard about what my first studio project should be. I kept coming back to the games that shaped my childhood: LAN parties with friends, playing [i]Diablo[/i] or [i]Titan Quest[/i] until sunrise, fueled by coffee and cola. Honestly, I was always more focused on saving the world, while my friends were all about the loot… :P In the end, I couldn’t think of a better reason to make a game than to follow my heart.[/p][p]So here we are! [b]This demo is an early, polished slice of Act 1[/b] — a first taste of what’s to come, released a few weeks ahead of Steam Next Fest in October.[/p][hr][/hr][h3][b]What you’ll find in the demo:[/b][/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45534103/d4f5cca674232ed4acf14fd6cbe953eaff3096fd.gif"][/img][/p][list][*][p]Fast-paced ARPG combat with two classes: Soldier & Adventurer[/p][/*][*][p]Local co-op support (up to 4 players)[/p][/*][*][p]A first look at the game’s 1930s pulp-adventure style, story, and atmosphere[/p][/*][/list][h3][b]What’s not here yet (but will be in Early Access):[/b][/h3][list][*][p]The final loot & inventory systems[/p][/*][*][p]Online co-op[/p][/*][*][p]Later Acts, additional classes, and the full skill card deck[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3][b]Looking Ahead – Early Access & Beyond[/b][/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45534103/d4441e31cb5be88180595009f6bba7ec68e14eeb.png"][/img][/p][p]I’ve chosen Early Access very deliberately — for me it isn’t a gimmick, it’s a necessity. I want to use it as it was meant to be: to find passionate players who want to help shape the game, and in full transparency, to help fund further development.[/p][list][*][p][b]Current status:[/b] Right now you have the demo. Later this year, the Early Access release will follow with the same two classes and the [i]whole of Act 1[/i].[/p][/*][*][p][b]The road ahead (next ~2 years):[/b] I’ll continue working full-time on the game, adding:[/p][list][*][p]Four more story Acts (main quest + sidequests)[/p][/*][*][p]3–4 additional classes, including at least 1 magic-focused character and 2 full melee characters[/p][/*][*][p]Online co-op[/p][/*][*][p]Full voice acting[/p][/*][*][p]And everything else you’d expect from a complete ARPG you can enjoy with friends[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p]And I want to be transparent about our studio’s stance on pricing and content. I know that when you buy Early Access, you’re spending your hard-earned money — often money you also need for essentials in a world where everything has gotten more expensive. That means when you buy [b]Under a Desert Sun[/b], you will get a [b]complete game[/b].[/p][list][*][p]No paid cosmetics[/p][/*][*][p]No seasonal passes that demand constant reinvestment[/p][/*][*][p]No microtransactions hidden in the corner[/p][/*][/list][p]The only possible extra cost in the future would be for proper expansions (DLCs), and those will always add substantial content: a new story Act, at least one new class, and a new set of items for every class.[/p][hr][/hr][h3][b]One last thing[/b][/h3][p]This demo is a work-in-progress, but it’s already playable and fun — and I’d really like to hear what you think. Leave feedback, tell us what parts you enjoyed, and if you feel like it, leave a review. Early impressions matter a lot as we head toward Next Fest, but most of all they help me understand what’s working and what still needs love.[/p][p]Thanks for giving this first adventure under the desert sun a try.[/p][p]– [b]Raymond @ Revolving Gear Studios[/b][/p]

notes.title: Under a Desert Sun: Seekers of the Cursed Vessel — FAQ
notes.notes:
[p]Hi everyone!
With Next Fest coming up and more people discovering the game, I thought it would be a good time to put together a Frequently Asked Questions list.
We’re posting it here once for visibility, but it will be [b]maintained and updated[/b] in the game’s forum section — it’s pinned at the top so you can always find the latest version.[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]Q: Is there a roadmap?[/b]
A: Yes! You can view the current development roadmap here: [/p][p][url="https://www.reddit.com/r/RevolvingGearStudios/comments/1m16qd3/under_a_desert_sun_seekers_of_the_cursed_vessel/"]https://www.reddit.com/r/RevolvingGearStudios/comments/1m16qd3/under_a_desert_sun_seekers_of_the_cursed_vessel/[/url][/p][p]
It will be updated as development progresses.[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]Q: What will the game cost?[/b]
A: Early Access will launch at a lower price to reward early supporters, with occasional discounts. The full release will see a price increase, but it will remain below the cost of most AAA titles — offering a fair price for the amount of content and the fact that this is an indie project. Even at full price, it will be more affordable than many comparable big-team ARPGs.[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]Q: Will there be paid cosmetics, seasons, or other types of paid services?[/b]
A: At Revolving Gear Studios, we believe players should receive a complete game and get exactly what they paid for. The only additional paid content will be story DLCs that may include new classes and extra content. (Disclaimer: The release of DLCs depends on how well the base game performs during and after Early Access.)[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]Q: Will there be a loot system?[/b]
A: Yes. The plan is to include a full loot system for weapons, gear, and similar items. While the complete system will not be ready for the demo or the first Early Access release, those versions will feature placed loot drops using an early version of the system.[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]Q: Are there difficulty settings?[/b]
A: Currently, only the normal difficulty is available. Additional difficulty options will be added during Early Access.[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]Q: How long will the final game be?[/b]
A: The goal is to have a four-act structure, with each act’s main story taking about 3–4 hours to complete. In addition, there will be side quests and other activities to explore throughout the world.[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]Q: Who is making this?[/b]
A: Hi! I’m Raymond, and I founded Revolving Gear Studios after working on a range of hobby projects and holding various interesting jobs in IT. While I’m the primary developer, I don’t really see the “solo dev” label as anything special — modern tools and collaboration with skilled artists, musicians, and other creatives make it entirely possible to build a game this way. I work with talented people on a contract basis to bring in the expertise and assets needed to bring the world of Under a Desert Sun to life.[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]Q: Can I beta test the game?[/b]
A: From time to time, we look for additional testers to try out early builds. Join the Discord to see when testing opportunities are available and how you can take part![/p][hr][/hr][p][b]Q: How does this compare to other ARPGs?[/b]
A: While I’m inspired by the classic ARPGs of the past, my focus is on a few key things. First, fun should always come before spreadsheets and extreme grinding — I want exploration and adventure to feel just as rewarding as leveling up. Second, the story should be engaging and central, not an afterthought. And finally, for me, ARPGs have always been about playing with friends — whether on LAN or online — and feeling like you’ve been somewhere else entirely. My goal is for players to finish a session thinking, “That was an adventure… let’s do it again!”[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]Q: How replayable will the game be?[/b]
A: In the final release, you’ll be able to carry your character into a new game, join someone else’s game, or move on to a higher difficulty level. If sales are strong, DLC will add even more content. I also plan to release updates with additional content based on the funding available — after the four acts and all core content are complete. As for the endgame, I’m still exploring what form it will take. What’s certain is that it will fit the game’s focus on immersion and fun over pure number-crunching.[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]Q: Will it run on Steam Deck?[/b][/p][p]A: Yes. The Steam Deck is one of the baseline benchmarks for the game. Currently, many areas run above 60 FPS on high settings. The aim is to maintain at least 40 FPS so players can cap the framerate at 40 for a smooth and consistent experience.[/p][p][/p][p]If your question isn’t listed here yet, feel free to ask in the comments or join the Discord community: [/p][p][url="https://discord.gg/g5fK7Df"]https://discord.gg/g5fK7Df[/url][/p][p][/p][p]Wishlist the game on Steam:
[/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3273880"][/dynamiclink][/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Under a Desert Sun: October Early Access Release October – Join Us at Next Fest!
notes.notes:
[p]Hey everyone![/p][p]I’m hard at work getting the demo ready for Steam Next Fest, and things are coming along nicely. The plan is to have a solid, playable chunk ready before the event—and then open up Early Access shortly after.[/p][p]Here’s a look at what’s been happening behind the scenes:[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Elemental effects now hit harder (and look cooler)[/b][/h2][previewyoutube="XvNYjR8uigM;full"][/previewyoutube][p]Elemental damage now packs more punch. Burning enemies like mages ignite immediately, and frozen foes will shatter into satisfying icy shards when smashed. Combat just got a whole lot juicier.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Dual wield skill is finalized and fully working[/b][/h2][previewyoutube="540v9Umq9Fg;full"][/previewyoutube][p]
One of the trickiest parts of our skill system is ensuring different abilities and elemental effects can combine seamlessly. Dual wielding posed a unique challenge—it affects how the player attacks, reloads, and triggers other effects. After a lot of tweaking and accounting for edge cases, it’s now working neatly with all elemental builds.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Main quest progression and new boss: the Flamethrower Baddy[/b][/h2][previewyoutube="z3O028wojoU;full"][/previewyoutube][p]
Development on the main quest continues, bringing new story content and fresh enemies—like this brand-new boss wielding a brutal flamethrower. The footage is from an early test map, but… you get the point. [i]WOOSH.[/i][/p][p][/p][h2][b]New enemy tech and UI polish[/b][/h2][previewyoutube="6sNk8syuW3g;full"][/previewyoutube][p]
I’ve also expanded general enemy behavior, adding projectile-throwing types to keep you on your toes. On top of that, the enemy name UI and various visual polish passes make everything look sharper and feel more refined.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Destructible environments (with loot!)[/b][/h2][previewyoutube="r_o0UvIZ_DE;full"][/previewyoutube][p]
Destructibles are in! Blowing things up is always fun, but they also help make the world feel alive—and sometimes they drop loot too. This is a small taste of the broader loot system that’s planned for expansion after the Early Access release.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Optional lore system: readable tomes and books[/b][/h2][previewyoutube="kdooV0LbUZc;full"][/previewyoutube][p]
For players who love world-building, I’ve added a system for reading tomes, scrolls, and ancient books. It’s completely optional, but offers rich lore if you want to dig deeper. And yes—it already looks pretty neat![/p][p][/p][h2][b]Major progress on the main story (but no spoilers)[/b][/h2][p]The largest additions are actually in the main quest and story… but I’m deliberately showing less of that for now. If you’re part of the Discord, you may have seen a few extra glimpses. For everyone else: it’s shaping up to be something special.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]👉 Don’t forget to wishlist [i]Under a Desert Sun: Seekers of the Cursed Vessel[/i][/b][/h2][p]It really helps with visibility and keeps you in the loop for Early Access and Next Fest![/p][h2][b]🎮 Want to see more and join the community?[/b][/h2][p]Hop into the [url="https://discord.gg/g5fK7Df"]Discord[/url] and chat with fellow adventurers, give feedback, or just lurk for sneak peeks.[/p]

notes.title: Under a Desert Sun: Seekers of the Cursed Vessel - progression update
notes.notes:
[p][b]Hello Seekers,[/b][/p][p]I thought it was a good moment to highlight some fresh progress! Development continues at full speed, starting with new environments and further work on the main quest. As some of you in the Discord already know, I use the main quest as a way to push myself to build new systems. I'm now at the point where everything leading up to the final moments of the main quest is functional—both tech-wise and, for the most part, art-wise.[/p][p]That means it was time to move the story forward again, which in turn forced me to create new areas, enemies, and gameplay features. One such feature is an improved [b]day and night system[/b], with smoother lighting transitions and smarter particle effects that fade out instead of abruptly disappearing. Below you'll find a quick idea of the new day/night features and a few in-editor screenshots showing the early stages of these new zones.[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="W8fBpR4LRIY;full"][/previewyoutube][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45534103/98681fabc5451329fa38a12406b8b82819de5a14.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45534103/d4345efc8b2f50bf2f8ad3fd06a0145ef4d8c1ac.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45534103/fc8caccf66faf6037f19803c5d2e466e21a1f55d.png"][/img][/p][p]Creating these new areas also meant designing [b]new enemy types[/b]—specifically ones that shoot projectiles! From Nazis who fire bullets to arcane mummies casting magical bolts, I needed to build the underlying tech. To get that going, I set up a test using our trusty mummy as a prototype. This allowed me to develop the full system: bullets, shooting and casting animations, and proper hit detection.[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="UoC7sk9P1rg;full"][/previewyoutube][p]Naturally, new areas also bring [b]more destructibles[/b]. And let’s be honest—breaking stuff in an ARPG is just fun. (As you can see from me thrashing around... purely professional testing, of course 😏)[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="r_o0UvIZ_DE;full"][/previewyoutube][p]On the technical side, [b]Steam Deck optimization remains a major goal[/b]. The game currently runs at a stable 45 FPS on Deck [i]without[/i] any upscaling like FSR—so you get a clean image and native visuals. To get there, I’ve upgraded several systems under the hood. Particle systems now fade naturally, enemy spawning uses pooled and distance-aware logic, and we've improved object [b]occlusion and visibility handling[/b] to keep things smooth when off-screen. These changes help across all platforms but especially make the Deck experience strong.[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]Join the [url="https://discord.gg/g5fK7Df"]Discord[/url][/b] for daily development discussions and behind-the-scenes previews.
And if you like what you see—[b][url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3273880/Under_a_Desert_Sun_Seekers_of_the_Cursed_Vessel/"]wishlist the game on Steam[/url][/b] to support the journey![/p]

notes.title: Under a Desert Sun: Seekers of the Cursed Vessel - Open world Day/night cycle
notes.notes: [p]🌞 A little behind-the-scenes look at the day-night system I’m building for Under a Desert Sun: Seekers of the Cursed Vessel.[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="W8fBpR4LRIY;full"][/previewyoutube][p]What makes it interesting? It’s quite efficient—each object simply registers to a central “sun” and gets updated on the time of day. Lights switch on and off with slight randomness, so environments feel natural rather than mechanical.[/p][p]Particles also don’t just snap off—they’re given soft transitions so they fade or “burn out” naturally, keeping the immersion intact.[/p][p]Always fun finding small touches that make the world feel more alive![/p]

notes.title: Under a Desert Sun: Seekers of the Cursed Vessel - Player UI improvements
notes.notes:
Hello Seekers!

As I’ve been working on all the class skills — both the Skillcard system and the special weapon skill tree — I realized it was time to overhaul the player UI as well.

Thanks to the wide variety of available skills, your characters can already differ quite a bit from each other, even if you pick the same class. I wanted to create a system where you can immediately see what you’re running:
– Which passive skill is active?
– Which active skill is currently slotted?
– Which elemental effect is applied to your bullets?

To solve this, I designed a set of small, elegant icons that integrate smoothly into the existing player UI. I deliberately avoided the typical bulky skill boxes you see in so many ARPGs — instead, I aimed for something more fluid and natural that fits seamlessly into the interface.

I hope you all like it! Let me know your thoughts.

Old player UI vs New:

notes.title: Performance Update
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45534103/0dbb010153a6582344408a76138adebabfd291d6.gif[/img]

Performance is key in a game like this. The Steam Deck is a prime target for testing, and beta revealed that enemies’ individual search-and-behavior loops were impacting performance. A full AI overhaul merged those cycles under a single “Mother” controller (yes, a nod to Alien’s onboard computer), unlocking (as you can see in the small vid above):

A stable 45 FPS on Deck—no FSR or other upscalers needed

Dramatically reduced CPU load during the wildest firefights

Rock-steady frame pacing even in the most demanding areas

Cracking this “Mother” system feels like mastering the more difficult parts of gamedesign. It is a truly proud achievement that brings the project right on target for Deck performance. More polish is coming—stay tuned!

notes.title: Progress progress progress
notes.notes:
[b]Hello everyone![/b]

I wanted to share a quick development update and show how things are progressing. The project is well on track for a summer Early Access release!     

As a reminder, the Early Access version will include Act 1 of the game and two playable classes. Eventually, we'll have more classes to pick from. Singleplayer and local co-op (up to 4 players) support is also included in early acces.

This past month, I’ve been hard at work on several exciting features and improvements, including:

[b]Character Select Scene Updates:[/b]

I’ve redone many of the small animation details in the character select scene to make it feel more polished and lively.

You’ll now also see the next two upcoming classes standing alongside the current roster. While they aren’t playable yet, I thought it would be a nice touch to already introduce them as part of the team!

New character select:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45534103/7981d6372d0c51de1abc99005742df83fd25693c.gif[/img]


[b]Skills System:[/b]
Both the Soldier and Adventurer classes (and all future classes) now feature two distinct skill systems:

The Skill Deck, a set of special ability cards tied to your class. You can slot up to 5 cards that heavily change how you play, adding new strategies and combat styles.

The Special Weapon Skill Tree, allowing you to adapt and modify your class’s unique special weapon for powerful customizations.

I’m happy to say that almost all skills are now implemented, and I’ll be dropping an overview video soon to show them in action! A small tease here below of frost bullets.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45534103/a75e54061bf590d11e1102df24a477019513e68e.gif[/img]

[b]UI Additions & Overhauls:[/b]

Various UI elements have been cleaned up or completely overhauled. For example, here’s a comparison between the old skill card system and the new version

Old skill system ui:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45534103/7e15d0657de73b13dc6d425c1a7b26fe49a1ce14.gif[/img]

New system (Cleaner!) + tutorial popup at the end!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45534103/b41185618c1f418d19ec859b15f3c561b88e1881.gif[/img]

Helpful hover labels now pop up when pointing at items to provide quick information.

A new, more elaborate tutorial system has been added that appears contextually when needed to help guide new players through the game.

[b]Technical Updates:[/b]

On the tech side, I’ve updated the save system to fully support all the new features and content added to the game. After every major addition, I make sure you can load back into the world and feel exactly where you left off—right at the correct point in the questline, looking the way you should, with your character fully intact!

[b]World Overhaul:[/b]

I’ve spent a lot of time reworking the world itself. Many graphics, textures, and particle effects have been overhauled to bring environments to life and make exploration even more engaging.

I think things are starting to look pretty good and connected:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45534103/1a34915f6dadf6b55cea1927fce71d52a55200ad.gif[/img]

I also added zone indicators that display the zone name when you enter a new area. This helps ground you more in the world and adds that satisfying sense of discovery as you explore!

Zone title test: (THe white block is a verrrrryyy obvious zone)
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45534103/b358665115e15d635f711005083a30b964c48bbb.gif[/img]


Thanks for following along and being part of this journey! Don’t forget to wishlist the game if you haven’t already and join our Discord to chat directly with the community:[url=https://discord.gg/g5fK7Df]Discord[/url]

More updates coming soon—and stay tuned for the upcoming skill overview video!

notes.title: Developer Update: Skill System Progress
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45534103/7e15d0657de73b13dc6d425c1a7b26fe49a1ce14.gif[/img]
Hi everyone! I’ve been working on further developing the skill system for the two playable classes currently in Under a Desert Sun: Seekers of the Cursed Vessel.

The goal is to give players meaningful choices through a layered approach to character customization:

On the right side of the screen, you'll find a classic Diablo II-style skill tree—both in appearance and philosophy. It’s deliberately old-school: no free respecs, so each decision matters and helps shape a distinct build.

Complementing that is a more flexible card slot system, which lets you adjust your playstyle on the fly. These cards introduce powerful modifiers and unique mechanics that can significantly alter your approach to combat and exploration.

The interaction between the two systems should create exciting variety. For example, one skill card available to the Adventurer disables rifle usage but unlocks the ability to dual wield pistols, enabling faster, close-range aggression.

The footage included in this update shows the player selecting a Frost or Burn bullet skill card—activating elemental bullets that apply freezing or burning effects to enemies on hit. This is just one of many ways skill cards can evolve your character’s abilities.

Choosing the frost bullet skill:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45534103/b3f02927a3d7dd296a24be121c144f37b12dd340.gif[/img]

Using the frost bullets:

notes.title: Exciting News: The Launch of Revolving Gear Studios!
notes.notes:
I have made the choice to start making video games and digital art full-time and have founded my own game studio, Revolving Gear Studios! This marks the beginning of an exciting journey—one that has been a lifelong dream of mine.

I've had many years of experience as a manager, head of development, developer, and in project execution and leadership, and I finally feel that I have the experience to take the plunge. Not to mention that I've always kept honing my skills as a game development hobbyist. My previous steam release as an example.

The first project under the new company, Under a Desert Sun: Seekers of the Cursed Vessel, is already in development, The progress can be tracked on this very steampage.

For those of you who know me and my previous works, you might recognize the name Under a Desert Sun from my earlier VR game. So yes indeed... I've started a franchise 😉.

Jokes aside, I wasn’t quite ready to let go of the desert theme just yet and wanted to tell more stories in the same universe. This time, I’ve decided to do so in the form of an action RPG, which you can play alone or with friends.

None of this would be possible without the unwavering support of my wife, family, and friends—thank you for always believing in me!

I’m looking forward to connecting with fellow developers, gamers, and creatives as I bring this vision to life. Let’s make something amazing together.
